title: test(hooks): add the missing self-test matrix for `guard-main-checkout.sh` (87 cases, ported)
body:
Fixes #6451

`guard-main-checkout.sh` was the only PreToolUse guard in this repo with no self-test, and it is the one both `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` §9 name **by path** as the mechanism enforcing worktree-first. Its Bash-side follow-on and `guard-shared-stash` both ship hermetic matrices; the primary guard had none, in either direction — a fail-open regression stops guarding the shared checkout in silence, a fail-closed one reads to an agent as a broken environment.

One new file: `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout.selftest.sh` (333 lines, mode 100755). Nothing else changed — see "the two legs that turned out to be no-ops" below.

## The port is verbatim, and that was measured before it was claimed

Ported from `objectstack-ai/objectstack:.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout.selftest.sh` @ `d63c8a2`, per the 2026-08-26 triage ruling on the card.

The two repos' hooks differ by **9 diff lines, all inside one comment block** (objectstack's copy carries an extra note above the heredoc). No executable line differs, and both `settings.json` route the identical `Edit|Write|NotebookEdit` matcher. So the sibling file was first run here **byte-for-byte unmodified**, through its own `GUARD_MAIN_CHECKOUT_HOOK` / `GUARD_MAIN_CHECKOUT_SETTINGS` indirection, pointed at this repo's hook and settings:

```
87 passed, 0 failed
```

**Zero cases needed adapting.** The only edits below the header are the two `KNOWN HOLE` sections, whose issue references are re-pointed at this repo's own cards (below); each keeps the sibling number as a cross-ref. `diff` against upstream is 4 hunks, all comment or `echo` label text.

## In place, and through the real CI step

```
$ .claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout.selftest.sh
87 passed, 0 failed                                     # exit 0
```

The `hook-selftests.yml` `run:` block, executed locally verbatim (`git rev-parse --short HEAD` = `3f5d6faf0`):

```
discovered 4 hook self-test(s):
  .claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.selftest.sh     121 passed, 0 failed   PASS
  .claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout.selftest.sh           87 passed, 0 failed   PASS
  .claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.selftest.sh            41 passed, 0 failed   PASS
  .claude/hooks/guard-tree-enum.selftest.sh               36 passed, 0 failed   PASS

Hook self-tests — all 4 ran and passed                  # step exit 0
```

## Non-vacuity — the matrix can go red against THIS repo's hook

Five mutation classes, each driven through the file's own footer recipe against a **scratch copy** in `$TMPDIR` (`GUARD_MAIN_CHECKOUT_HOOK`); the real hook is never touched, and each mutation was confirmed to have landed on disk by a marker grep count going `1 -> 0` before the reading was accepted:

| mutation of a scratch copy | result |
|---|---|
| drop the `*/worktrees/*) exit 0` arm | `62 passed, 25 failed` |
| replace `dirname "$file"` with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` | `52 passed, 35 failed` |
| drop the `OS_ALLOW_MAIN_EDITS` line | `85 passed, 2 failed` |
| final `exit 2` becomes `exit 0` | `45 passed, 42 failed` |
| rename the key in the jq-less grep fallback | `83 passed, 4 failed` |

`git diff --stat` on `guard-main-checkout.sh` is empty after all five; only the new untracked matrix appeared.

## Two defects the port surfaced — filed, not fixed

Both `KNOWN HOLE` sections reproduce here identically, so they are this repo's defects too and now have this repo's cards. Per the card's fence, this PR **pins today's behaviour and says the hole out loud**; it does not change the guard.

- #7259 — any git-dir path containing `/worktrees/` reads as a linked worktree, so a primary checkout living under a dir named `worktrees` is unguarded, and **by depth** (git prints a relative git-dir at a toplevel, absolute from a subdirectory). 4 cases pinned.
- #7260 — `NotebookEdit`'s path key is `notebook_path`, which the hook never reads, so every notebook edit is judged by `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` instead of by the file. Wrong in 4 of 5 measured directions, including two fail-open ones. 5 cases pinned.

Neither card is closed by this PR; #7259 and #7260 remain open, and each names the mechanical edit to this matrix that its fix implies.

## The two legs of the triage ruling that turned out to be no-ops

The 2026-08-26 triage named three legs. The port is leg 1. The other two were hypotheses, re-checked against today's tree:

- **"wire it into `hook-selftests.yml`"** — already automatic. The step discovers matrices with `find .claude/hooks -type f -name '*.selftest.sh'` since #7019, and the run above shows it picking up all four with no workflow edit. The header even anticipates this card by name at `:51`.
- **"refresh the header's stale recorded counts (100/32 vs the tree's 121/41)"** — the header now **forbids** exactly that. `:95-101`: *"Those counts stay, and the distinction is deliberate (objectui#6089): a measurement is HISTORY. It is read together with its date and its sha, and a matrix that grows afterwards does not make it false — it makes it older. Both have grown since (121 and 41 as of 2026-08-31, plus a third matrix), which is exactly what a dated measurement is allowed to do."* That second sentence, itself dated, landed after the triage comment was written and already records the current figures. Editing either would convert a dated measurement into a live claim, which is the shape the same header rejects for step names. The live count is published by the thing that cannot get it wrong: the step prints how many matrices it discovered.

So the workflow is untouched, deliberately. The hook header is untouched too, matching upstream — objectstack's `guard-main-checkout.sh` carries no self-test pointer either, despite having had the matrix for longer.

## Gates

Derived from the workflow files that can see `.claude/hooks/**` (only `hook-selftests.yml` carries a matching `paths:` filter; the rest are unfiltered). All run on `3f5d6faf0`, exit code captured before any pipe:

| gate | verdict line |
|---|---|
| `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout.selftest.sh` | `87 passed, 0 failed` (exit 0) |
| the other three matrices | `121 / 41 / 36 passed, 0 failed` (all PASS) |
| `check-control-bytes` | `✅  check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 5997 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `check-shell-escape-residue` | `✅  check-shell-escape-residue: OK (4/4 root(s) resolved …)` |
| `check-changeset-presence` | `✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` |
| `check-upstream-port-parity` | `✓ … 2 ported file(s) match objectstack-ai/objectstack@bf10debd5 modulo their declared divergences.` |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --self-test` | `OK check-governed-queue-guard self-test: 132 cases pass` |

Two honest notes on scope rather than green-washing them:

- `check-shell-escape-residue` resolves `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `skills/` and `content/docs/` — **not** `.claude/hooks/`. Its green is true and says nothing about this file. **NOT MEASURED**, not passed.
- `check-control-bytes` *does* cover it (the file is tracked and inside the 5997), and a manual `grep -naP '[\x00-…]'` over the new file independently returns 0 hits.

**No changeset owed** — quoted above; `.claude/**` publishes nothing. This repo declares that with an empty-frontmatter changeset where one is needed and has no `skip-changeset` mechanism, and the presence gate is green without one, so none was added.

## Review posture

`.claude/**` is governed surface: **draft, human merge only.** Not marked ready, not enqueued, no auto-merge armed.
